questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a charge from a payment?
choices: They are always identical
A charge is an amount listed by the organization, while payment is what the payer and patient actually remit under applicable terms
Payment is always higher than cost
A charge measures clinical value
questions.explanation: Costs, charges, allowed amounts, payments, and patient liability are distinct; billed charges do not by themselves show revenue or value.

questions.question: Which set belongs in a balanced practice dashboard?
choices: Visit count only
Charges and social-media followers only
Quality, safety, access, patient experience, workforce, equity, compliance, and financial sustainability
Clinician speed only
questions.explanation: A single productivity or financial measure can hide harm, burden, or inequity. Sustainable high-value care requires a balanced set of outcomes.

questions.question: A payer denies a clinically appropriate service. What is the best response?
choices: Confirm the indication and policy, discuss patient cost exposure, use authorization or appeal pathways when justified, and never change facts to obtain payment
Submit a different diagnosis that was not present
Tell the patient coverage and clinical value are identical
Ignore the denial
questions.explanation: Coverage and clinical appropriateness are related but distinct; legitimate appeals use accurate evidence and documentation rather than misrepresentation.

questions.question: Which arrangement requires compliance and legal review before proceeding?
choices: Buying routine office paper at market price
Providing a patient with a receipt
Reviewing a quality dashboard
Accepting vendor payments or free equipment linked to referral volume
questions.explanation: Remuneration connected to referrals or business generation can create fraud-and-abuse and conflict-of-interest risk and needs authoritative review.

questions.question: Why is opportunity cost important in a business case?
choices: It replaces all direct cost estimates
It identifies what other valuable work or benefit is forgone when limited resources are committed
It proves a project will be profitable
It is the same as a billed charge
questions.explanation: Resources used for one activity cannot be used elsewhere; hidden staff time and displaced work can materially change value and feasibility.

questions.question: A clinic's visit count is low because clinicians perform extensive nonvisit care coordination. What is the best management response?
choices: Assume the clinicians are inefficient
Require unsupported higher coding
Measure complexity, coordination, inbox work, outcomes, access, staffing, payer design, and workload before redesigning the model
Eliminate all follow-up calls
questions.explanation: Visit count alone ignores essential work and patient complexity. A balanced workflow and financial analysis is needed before changing care.

questions.question: Which statement about capitation or value-based payment is most accurate?
choices: It can support prevention and coordination but requires safeguards against undertreatment, risk selection, weak measures, and inequity
It eliminates financial incentives
It guarantees better outcomes
It has no need for risk adjustment
questions.explanation: Prospective and value-based models can improve care design but also shift risk and create avoidance or undertreatment incentives.

questions.question: What should occur when a billing audit identifies a possible overpayment pattern?
choices: Delete the original documentation
Ignore small errors
Change prior notes without an amendment trail
Preserve records, stop ongoing risk when safe, notify the authorized compliance channel, quantify accurately, and follow correction and refund requirements
questions.explanation: Suspected overpayments require transparent, timely, policy-based investigation and correction—not concealment or improper record alteration.

questions.question: What is the best description of a strong healthcare business case?
choices: A claim that savings are guaranteed
A transparent analysis of need, alternatives, workflow, costs, payment, assumptions, risks, implementation, and clinical, access, equity, and workforce outcomes
A list of revenue without expenses
A marketing plan without compliance review
questions.explanation: A credible case integrates financial and operational assumptions with patient outcomes, implementation requirements, uncertainty, and risk.

questions.question: A practice wants to spread a new care-management service after a promising pilot. What should it do?
choices: Hire system-wide before reviewing results
Stop measuring after the first month
Validate outcomes and assumptions, test capacity and payer variation, monitor workload and equity, and scale with clear ownership and contingency plans
Depend on one champion indefinitely
questions.explanation: Scaling requires validated clinical and financial performance under varied conditions, adequate infrastructure, monitoring, and sustainable ownership.
